criteria.query: In second-language (L2) writers receiving instruction, what are the effects of written corrective feedback (teacher-provided, peer-provided or automated) on writing accuracy, revision behaviour and learner engagement, compared with no feedback or alternative feedback conditions?
exclusion_criteria: Feedback is exclusively oral (spoken corrective feedback in speaking tasks) rather than written
Participants are first-language writers only, with no second- or foreign-language writing component
Non-empirical contributions such as editorials, book reviews, position pieces or conference announcements
The study concerns feedback on non-writing skills (e.g. pronunciation, listening, vocabulary tests) only
inclusion_criteria: Empirical study (experimental, quasi-experimental, observational or case study) or a research synthesis of empirical studies
Participants are second- or foreign-language writers (any age or proficiency level) in an instructed setting
The study examines written corrective feedback or written feedback on L2 writing, whether from a teacher, a peer or an automated tool
Reports at least one outcome concerning writing accuracy, revision or uptake, learner engagement, or beliefs and preferences about feedback
